3. The suit was decreed on contest and the decree was affirmed in appeal. The Chairman took a revision to the High Court Division, Civil Revision No.1178 of 1993, against the said decree and a learned Single Judge by the impugned judgment and order dated 9 July, 1997 made the Rule absolute and set aside the concurrent decree. 

 4. It appears from the impugned judgment that it was argued on behalf of the defendant that the suit was not maintainable on the ground that prior notice as required under section 78 of the Local Government (Union Parishads) Ordinance, 1983 was not served upon the Union Parishad before instituting the suit. Secondly, it was argued that the plaintiff not having prayed for any consequential relief in the suit the same was hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. In support of both the contentions several decisions were cited by the defendant. The learned Judge accepted both the contentions and, as already noticed, set aside the decree passed in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner. Now this petition for leave to appeal from the decision of' the High Court Division. Syed Ziaul Karim, learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the petitioner's appointment, training, terms and conditions of service are regulated by the Union Council (Village Police Force) Rules 1968 and, as such, the provision of section 78 of the Local Government (Union Parishads) Ordinance, 1983 is not applicable to him.
